About Bitdeer:

Bitdeer is a world-leading technology company for Bitcoin mining and AI cloud.

Bitdeer is committed to providing comprehensive Bitcoin mining solutions for its customers. Apart from designing industry-leading ASIC chips and manufacturing mining rigs, the Group handles complex processes involved in computing across the value chain. This includes equipment procurement, transport logistics, datacenter design and construction, equipment management, and network and facility operations. Bitdeer also offers advanced cloud capabilities to customers with a high demand for artificial intelligence.

Headquartered in Singapore, Bitdeer operates globally with a diversified 3 GW energy portfolio, and deploys Bitcoin mining and HPC datacenters in the United States, Bhutan, Norway, Canada, Malaysia, and Ethiopia.

About the role

We are seeking a Billing Analyst to own the accuracy of usage-to-invoice for Bitdeer AI's Model-as-a-Service platform, making sure every token processed, GPU-second consumed, and fine-tuning job run is metered correctly and reflected faithfully on customer invoices. Today, raw inference usage events, GPU-hour allocations, and tiered per-token pricing rules live across several internal metering pipelines and billing systems that do not always agree, which produces recurring month-end discrepancies between what customers were charged and what they actually consumed, and slows down the process of issuing service credits when GPU faults or capacity outages interrupt a customer's workload. This role closes that gap: reconciling usage data against billing records line by line, maintaining and evolving the pricing models that translate consumption into charges, and calculating fair, well-documented credits when infrastructure failures affect a tenant's jobs. The person who thrives here is comfortable moving between spreadsheets, SQL queries, and billing-platform configuration in the same afternoon, treats a small reconciliation gap as a signal worth chasing rather than a rounding error, and can explain a pricing or credit decision clearly to both an engineer debugging a metering pipeline and a customer disputing an invoice.

What you will be responsible for:

  • Usage-to-Invoice Reconciliation: Reconcile raw metering data, including token counts, GPU-seconds, storage, and API call volumes, against billed line items on the MaaS platform every billing cycle. Investigate variances between usage logs and invoiced amounts down to the account and job level, tracing them to metering pipeline bugs, pricing misconfigurations, or timing gaps. Document root causes and drive fixes with engineering and finance-systems teams so recurring discrepancies do not reappear the following month.
  • Pricing Model Maintenance: Maintain and help evolve the pricing models that convert raw consumption into customer charges, including per-token rates for chat and embeddings, per-GPU-hour rates for fine-tuning and dedicated capacity, and tiered or committed-use discounts. Model the revenue impact of proposed pricing changes before they ship, and validate that pricing configuration in the billing system matches what product and sales have committed to customers, catching mismatches before they reach an invoice.
  • GPU-Fault Service Credits: Calculate and issue service credits when GPU faults, node failures, or capacity outages interrupt customer inference or training jobs, using SLA terms and incident timelines from infrastructure and reliability teams. Build a consistent, auditable methodology for sizing credits so similar incidents are treated the same way across customers, and track credit issuance so it can be reported as a cost of reliability rather than absorbed silently into revenue.
  • Billing Data Quality and Anomaly Detection: Monitor usage and billing pipelines for anomalies such as duplicate metering events, missing usage records, or pricing-tier misapplication before invoices go out. Build recurring checks and lightweight dashboards that flag unusual spend patterns or metering gaps early, and partner with data engineering to close instrumentation gaps at the source rather than patching them downstream every cycle.
  • Billing Support and Dispute Resolution: Serve as the analytical backstop for customer-facing billing disputes, pulling underlying usage evidence and walking account managers or support through exactly how a charge or credit was calculated. Turn recurring dispute themes into proposed changes to pricing logic, invoice presentation, or metering granularity so the same question does not need to be re-litigated for the next customer.

How you will stand out:

  • Bring 3+ years of experience in billing operations, revenue operations, or financial analysis at a cloud infrastructure, SaaS, or other usage-metered business, with direct exposure to consumption-based pricing.
  • Demonstrate strong SQL skills for querying usage and billing data across large event volumes, and comfort working in a data warehouse such as Snowflake, BigQuery, or Redshift to reconcile metering pipelines against billed output.
  • Show hands-on experience with at least one usage-based or subscription billing platform, such as Stripe Billing, Zuora, Chargebee, Metronome, or Orb, including how rating, invoicing, and credit memos are configured.
  • Have working knowledge of how GPU and compute-based pricing works, including per-token, per-GPU-hour, and tiered or committed-use models, and be able to translate SLA terms into concrete credit calculations.
  • Be comfortable working across engineering, finance, and customer-facing teams under ambiguity, tracing a billing discrepancy from a customer invoice back to a raw metering event without a fully documented data model to lean on.
  • Bring advanced spreadsheet modeling skills in Excel or Google Sheets for one-off reconciliations and pricing scenario analysis, plus basic scripting in Python or a similar language to automate recurring checks.

What you will experience working with us:

  • A culture that values authenticity and diversity of thoughts and backgrounds;
  • An inclusive and respectable environment with open workspaces and exciting start-up spirit;
  • Fast-growing company with the chance to network with industrial pioneers and enthusiasts;
  • Ability to contribute directly and make an impact on the future of the digital asset industry;

  • Personal accountability, autonomy, fast growth, and learning opportunities;

About Bitdeer:

Bitdeer is a world-leading technology company for Bitcoin mining and AI cloud.

Bitdeer is committed to providing comprehensive Bitcoin mining solutions for its customers. Headquartered in Singapore, Bitdeer operates globally with a diversified 3 GW energy portfolio, and deploys Bitcoin mining and HPC datacenters in the United States, Bhutan, Norway, Canada, Malaysia, and Ethiopia.

About the role

We are seeking a Billing Analyst to own the correctness of usage-to-invoice accounting for our multi-tenant GPU cloud, sitting at the intersection of finance, product, and the AI Cloud Kubernetes engineering team. As GPU capacity scales across regions, GPU types, commitment tiers, and spot/on-demand pricing, the SKU matrix behind our billing grows more complex faster than any spreadsheet can track cleanly, and every unresolved discrepancy is a customer-facing dollar amount. This role designs and maintains the pricing models that translate raw platform usage into billable line items, reconciles metered consumption against generated billing statements to catch drift before it reaches a customer invoice, and administers GPU-fault credits — determining and applying the correct credit when GPU hardware or host failures interrupt billed usage. The work requires fluency in how usage events flow from the Kubernetes platform's metering pipeline through rating and aggregation into the ledger, without requiring the person to build that pipeline. You will work with engineering to specify metering requirements and validate outputs, with finance to define pricing and credit policy, and with product to model new SKUs as GPU offerings evolve. This is a domain-analyst role, not a software engineering role, but one where analytical rigor and fluency with usage data at scale are non-negotiable.

What you will be responsible for:

    • Pricing Model Design: Design and maintain pricing models across the full GPU SKU matrix — GPU type, region, commitment tier, and spot versus on-demand — ensuring every combination maps to a correct, unambiguous rate. Model new pricing structures such as tiered discounts, commitment-based rates, and burst pricing as new GPU offerings and contract types launch. Translate commercial pricing decisions from product and finance into rules the metering and billing systems can execute without ambiguity.
    • Metering and Usage Analysis: Analyze usage data emitted by the platform's metering pipeline — GPU-hours, node-hours, storage, network egress — to validate that recorded consumption matches actual customer activity across clusters and namespaces. Define the metering requirements engineering must capture, including granularity, tagging, and timestamps, so usage attributes correctly to the right tenant, SKU, and billing period. Flag metering coverage gaps, such as partial-hour billing or multi-GPU pod scheduling, before they surface as invoice disputes.
    • Billing Reconciliation: Reconcile metered usage against generated billing statements and payment records line by line, isolating drift caused by rating errors, pricing misconfigurations, timing mismatches, or metering gaps. Build and maintain reconciliation processes that catch discrepancies before invoices go out, and drive root-cause investigations with engineering when drift recurs. Maintain an auditable trail from raw usage event to final invoice line for every disputed or high-value account.
    • GPU-Fault Credit Administration: Administer the GPU-fault credit process end to end — determining eligibility when hardware or host failures interrupt billed usage, calculating the correct credit against the affected SKU and time window, and applying it accurately to the customer's account. Maintain clear, auditable credit policies that scale as fault volume grows, and work with infrastructure/SRE teams to obtain the incident and downtime data needed to substantiate each decision. Track credit issuance trends to surface systemic reliability issues worth escalating to engineering leadership.
    • Cross-Functional Partnership: Serve as the billing domain expert bridging finance, product, and the AI Cloud Kubernetes engineering team, translating commercial requirements into concrete metering and billing specifications. Review new product and pricing launches for billing readiness before go-live, confirming SKUs, metering, and credit logic are fully defined. Escalate systemic billing risks, such as undercharging or credit leakage, with data-backed analysis rather than anecdote.
    • Process and Controls: Build repeatable, documented processes for month-end close, invoice review, and credit issuance so billing operations scale without proportional headcount growth. Establish audit checkpoints that catch billing errors before customer-facing exposure, treating every invoicing mistake as a trust and revenue risk. Maintain pricing rules, SKU definitions, and credit policies as the documented source of truth shared by engineering and finance.

    How you will stand out:

      • Bring 3+ years of experience in billing, revenue operations, or financial analysis for a usage-based or consumption-priced product, ideally in cloud infrastructure, GPU/compute, or another metered-usage business. Demonstrate a track record of owning pricing model design and billing reconciliation for a product with a non-trivial SKU matrix.
      • Show strong analytical fluency with usage and billing data — comfortable working directly in SQL or spreadsheets against large usage-event datasets to identify drift, audit invoices, and validate metering output, rather than relying solely on pre-built dashboards. Bring demonstrated experience reconciling metered consumption against invoices at scale, with an eye for catching subtle discrepancies before they reach customers.
      • Have direct experience with credit, adjustment, or SLA-remediation processes in a usage-based billing context — designing or administering credit policy, calculating credit amounts against complex rate structures, and maintaining full auditability of every adjustment.
      • Be comfortable working cross-functionally with engineering to specify metering requirements and validate that platform usage data is fit for billing purposes, without needing to write the underlying metering code yourself. Familiarity with how cloud or Kubernetes usage is measured — compute-hours, GPU-hours, node- or pod-level attribution — is a strong plus.
      • Bring precise, structured communication and documentation habits. The pricing rules, SKU definitions, and credit policies you own must be legible to finance, product, and engineering alike, since ambiguity here becomes a customer-facing billing error.

      What you will experience working with us:

      • A culture that values authenticity and diversity of thoughts and backgrounds;
      • An inclusive and respectable environment with open workspaces and exciting start-up spirit;
      • Fast-growing company with the chance to network with industrial pioneers and enthusiasts;
      • Ability to contribute directly and make an impact on the future of the digital asset industry;
      • Involvement in new projects, developing processes/systems;
      • Personal accountability, autonomy, fast growth, and learning opportunities;
      • Attractive welfare benefits and developmental opportunities such as training and mentoring.
